title.en: CRU policy scope and 1 MVA de-minimis threshold

applicability.scope: All data centres seeking a new connection to the electricity network under CRU/2025236.
thresholds: MIC below 1 MVA: only locational capacity assessment applies under this policy.
MIC equal to or above 1 MVA: renewable and generation-related requirements apply, subject to the relevant MIC band.
location_conditions: The System Operators retain authority to determine whether the requested connection can be accommodated.

screening_logic.rule: First classify the project by Maximum Import Capacity (MIC). Do not apply the 1–<10 MVA or ≥10 MVA requirements until MIC is documented.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: If MIC, application type, or current capacity evidence is unknown, the grid screen is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rather than pass.
screening_logic.agent_action: Request an applicant load schedule and the latest EirGrid/ESB Networks locational assessment before presenting a site as investable.

content.en: CRU/2025236 applies exclusively to data centres seeking to connect to Ireland’s electricity network. The policy sets a de-minimis level of 1 MVA. Below 1 MVA, the System Operators (SOs) should still consider whether the requested location is constrained or unconstrained and may decide whether the connection can be accommodated; the other policy requirements do not apply. At or above 1 MVA, the policy’s capacity-band requirements apply. MIC means Maximum Import Capacity and should be treated as the core classification input for preliminary screening.

title.en: Data centres from 1 MVA to below 10 MVA: autoproducer requirement

applicability.scope: A data centre with MIC equal to or above 1 MVA and below 10 MVA applying for a new electricity connection.
thresholds: 1 MVA ≤ MIC < 10 MVA.
An autoproducer unit must meet 100% of the demand site's MIC on a de-rated basis.
Associated renewable generation contribution, up to 80% of annual demand, may be reflected on a de-rated basis against the autoproducer requirement.
location_conditions: The applicable generation asset must be operational for the duration of the connection.

screening_logic.rule: For 1–<10 MVA, require documentary evidence that an autoproducer will meet 100% of MIC on a de-rated basis and participate in the wholesale electricity market. Do not count nameplate capacity without a de-rating assessment.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: If the de-rated capacity is below MIC or market participation has no credible plan, mark CONDITIONAL / material grid-connection risk.
screening_logic.agent_action: Request a technical de-rating calculation, operating-duration commitment, market-participation route, and any renewable contribution calculation.

content.en: For data centres with MIC from 1 MVA to below 10 MVA, CRU/2025236 requires an autoproducer unit that meets 100% of the demand site’s MIC on a de-rated basis and participates in the wholesale electricity market. If the autoproducer requirement is met, no separate Mandatory Demand Curtailment provision is required under this policy. Associated renewable generation contribution, up to 80% of annual demand, may be reflected on a de-rated basis against the autoproducer requirement. The de-rated capacity must at minimum meet MIC and be operational for the duration of the connection.

title.en: Data centres at or above 10 MVA: dispatchable generation or storage

applicability.scope: A data centre with MIC equal to or above 10 MVA applying for a new electricity connection.
thresholds: MIC ≥ 10 MVA.
De-rated dispatchable onsite or proximate generation and/or storage capacity must match the site's MIC.
The connection cannot become operational or ramp to full MIC before the associated dispatchable asset is delivered and operational.
location_conditions: Generation or storage may be onsite or proximate; it must be separately connected and metered.

screening_logic.rule: For a ≥10 MVA project, test whether the de-rated dispatchable generation and/or storage capacity equals or exceeds the ramped or enduring MIC for the entire connection term, with a credible delivery sequence before energisation or full ramp-up.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: If the asset is absent, not proximate/onsite, undersized after de-rating, lacks separate metering, or is scheduled after full ramp-up, mark STOP for the current connection strategy or CONDITIONAL if the design can be revised before application.
screening_logic.agent_action: Require engineering evidence, a de-rating methodology, metering and connection topology, a market participation plan, and a construction schedule tied to the data centre ramp profile.

content.en: For data centres with MIC equal to or greater than 10 MVA, CRU/2025236 requires dispatchable onsite or proximate generation and/or storage capacity matching the site's MIC, subject to de-rating requirements. The asset must be separately connected and metered and must participate in the wholesale electricity market. The associated renewable generation contribution may be acknowledged, up to 80% of annual demand, on a de-rated basis against this requirement. The data-centre connection cannot be operational or ramp to full MIC without delivery of the associated onsite or proximate generation. The de-rated capacity must at least meet the ramped or enduring MIC and be operational for the connection duration.

title.en: 80% additional renewable electricity requirement and six-year glide path

applicability.scope: A data centre with MIC equal to or above 1 MVA applying for a new electricity connection under CRU/2025236.
thresholds: At least 80% of annual demand must be met with additional renewable electricity generated in the Republic of Ireland.
The developer has a six-year glide path from the demand site's energisation to meet the annual 80% requirement.
Generation previously or currently contracted under REFIT, RESS or ORESS cannot be used to satisfy the additionality requirement.
location_conditions: The renewable electricity must be generated in the Republic of Ireland.

screening_logic.rule: Calculate 80% of forecast annual demand. Accept only a credible plan for additional renewable projects located in the Republic of Ireland, excluding generation that has been or is contracted under named support mechanisms. Measure the six-year period from energisation, not land acquisition or planning consent.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: If 80% cannot be evidenced within the six-year glide path, or the scheme is not additional Irish renewable generation, mark CONDITIONAL / connection-policy non-compliance risk.
screening_logic.agent_action: Ask for project/contract evidence, expected annual output, energisation milestones, Irish location evidence, REFIT/RESS/ORESS status, and an annual matching calculation. Do not state that a CPPA is the only permissible legal mechanism.

content.en: CRU/2025236 requires data centres with MIC at or above the de-minimis level to meet at least 80% of annual demand with additional renewable electricity generated in the Republic of Ireland. A six-year glide path runs from the demand site’s energisation to meet that annual requirement. To meet the additionality test, renewable generation previously or currently contracted through existing support mechanisms, including REFIT, RESS and ORESS, cannot be used. The CRU states that developers may develop qualifying generation directly or contract with other parties; the decision does not prescribe a corporate power purchase agreement as the sole route.

title.en: Locational network constraints are assessed site by site

record.authority: Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU); EirGrid and ESB Networks as System Operators

applicability.scope: All data-centre connection applications, including those below the 1 MVA de-minimis level for the locational assessment element.
thresholds: No fixed Dublin-wide numerical probability or blanket capacity prohibition is stated in CRU/2025236.
The System Operators must assess whether the requested connection is in a constrained or unconstrained location.
location_conditions: Assessment concerns the proposed data-centre connection and associated generation location on the electricity network.
System Operators are to publish current and future locational capacity/constraint information.

screening_logic.rule: Treat locational constraint as a current, site-specific hard gate. A historic regional restriction or a general Dublin claim is not a substitute for the latest System Operator evidence.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: If current official constrained-area evidence is missing, return VERIFY / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. If the System Operator evidence indicates the application cannot be accommodated, return STOP for the proposed connection route.
screening_logic.agent_action: Retrieve the latest constrained-area overview and obtain a pre-application assessment. Log the publication date and geographic matching method; escalate material uncertainty to EirGrid/ESB Networks.

content.en: CRU/2025236 directs the System Operators to consider whether a requested data-centre connection is in a constrained or unconstrained location on the electricity network. This replaces the earlier broad regional approach with an assessment focused on the details and location of the specific application. The System Operators decide whether a connection can be accommodated and must publish regular, up-to-date information on existing and anticipated capacity and network constraints. EirGrid’s demand-connections page publishes the Data Centre Connection Offer Process and Policy Version 3 and a Data Centre Constrained Area Overview document. A screening agent must not translate this into a deterministic statement that all uncontracted Dublin sites have near-zero connection probability.

title.en: Data-centre connection process and application evidence

applicability.scope: New data-centre connection applicants using EirGrid’s published data-centre process.
thresholds: For general demand connections below 20 MVA at one location, EirGrid directs customers to ESB Networks; EirGrid handles larger general demand connections.
For data centres, use the dedicated data-centre materials published under DCCOPP Version 3 rather than assuming the general demand process determines the applicable policy.
location_conditions: The relevant System Operator and process depend on the connection characteristics and the applicable data-centre process.

screening_logic.rule: Before recommending paid engineering work or application submission, confirm that the project can provide the dedicated data-centre application form and associated documents specified by EirGrid’s current process.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: A missing technical, land, confidentiality or Grid Code document produces VERIFY / application-readiness gap, not a finding that the site itself is infeasible.
screening_logic.agent_action: Create an application-readiness checklist from the current DCCOPP version, data-centre technical assessment paper, constrained-area overview and application form. Always check document version and replacement notices.

title.en: Large Energy User Action Plan and Green Energy Parks

record.authority: Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment; Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment

applicability.scope: Very large, energy-intensive developments, including hyperscale data centres, in Ireland.
thresholds: LEAP is a plan-led policy approach, not an automatic site-specific planning permission or grid connection right.
The government describes green energy parks as co-locating energy-intensive industry with indigenous renewable energy, including offshore wind.
location_conditions: Projects in strategically prepared locations are policy-preferred for very large developments.
LEAP does not preclude energy-intensive developments outside strategic locations before or beyond 2030, subject to existing planning arrangements.

screening_logic.rule: For hyperscale or similarly large projects, score genuine co-location with renewable-resource and infrastructure planning as a positive policy signal. Do not treat a site outside a prospective green energy park as automatically prohibited.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: Lack of strategic-location alignment should cause DEPRIORITISE / policy-fit risk for very large projects, while the statutory connection and planning tests remain separate.
screening_logic.agent_action: Check the current National Planning Statement, any officially identified green-energy-park sites, planning designations, renewable-resource linkage and supporting infrastructure plans before assigning a policy-fit score.

content.en: Ireland’s Cabinet-approved Large Energy User Action Plan (LEAP) sets out a plan-led approach for large energy-intensive developments, including data centres. The policy’s core approach is to locate new large energy demand near renewable energy sources. It envisages green energy parks that co-locate energy-intensive industrial development with indigenous renewable energy, including offshore wind, and notes that a forthcoming National Planning Statement will inform the approach. LEAP explicitly does not preclude energy-intensive development outside strategic plan-led locations; such projects remain possible under existing planning arrangements. Therefore, green-energy-park alignment is a high-value policy signal, not a standalone legal exclusion test.

title.en: CRU/2025236 does not create a new gas-connection or biomethane rule

applicability.scope: Data-centre projects considering gas supply, gas-fired dispatchable assets, biomethane or green hydrogen as part of the connection strategy.
thresholds: CRU/2025236 introduced no new decision for gas-network connections.
The decision records ongoing work with Gas Networks Ireland on a potential interruptible gas-capacity product and proposes later consultation.
location_conditions: Any gas-system requirement must be assessed under applicable current gas rules, not inferred from the electricity connection decision.

screening_logic.rule: Do not award legal-compliance credit merely because a project proposes biomethane, green hydrogen, or gas-fired backup. Check the current gas connection and environmental rules separately.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: If the business case assumes that CRU/2025236 grants gas capacity or provides a mandated/preferred biomethane route, mark VERIFY / unsupported regulatory assumption.
screening_logic.agent_action: Route gas and fuel strategy to a separate Gas Networks Ireland and environmental-permitting review; retain a clear distinction between renewable-electricity compliance and fuel decarbonisation claims.

content.en: In CRU/2025236, the CRU acknowledges interaction between electricity and gas networks and notes that it consulted on biomethane and green hydrogen in relation to gas-fired large-energy-user demand. However, the final decision expressly states that it is not introducing any new decisions relating to connections to the gas network as part of that review. It refers to CRU engagement with Gas Networks Ireland on a potential interruptible gas-capacity product and possible separate consultation. Consequently, the electricity connection policy should not be represented as creating an explicit biomethane preference or a new gas-connection entitlement for data centres.

title.en: EU data-centre sustainability reporting and KPI methodology

applicability.scope: Operators of data centres in the EU with an installed information-technology power demand of at least 500 kW.
thresholds: Installed IT power demand ≥ 500 kW.
The operator must communicate the information and key performance indicators in the regulation to the European database, subject to the applicable reporting regime.
location_conditions: Every data centre at a different physical location is to have a separate set of information and KPIs, including on a campus.

screening_logic.rule: If installed IT power demand is at least 500 kW, open an EU reporting-compliance workstream. Capture data architecture for the Annex metrics at design stage rather than attempting to reconstruct it after operation begins.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: If a qualifying project lacks KPI ownership, metering or data-collection design, mark CONDITIONAL / operational-compliance readiness gap. This is not, by itself, a pre-construction connection refusal criterion.
screening_logic.agent_action: Assign a reporting entity; plan metering and governance for energy consumption, power utilisation, temperature set points, waste-heat use, water use and renewable-energy use; keep each physical site separately reportable.

content.en: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 is in force and establishes the first phase of a common Union data-centre rating scheme. It sets the information and key performance indicators to be communicated to the European database by operators of data centres with installed IT power demand of at least 500 kW, together with common monitoring and calculation methodology. The regulation describes this as the basis for data-centre sustainability indicators. The European Commission explains that the Energy Efficiency Directive introduced monitoring and reporting of data-centre energy performance; the reported KPIs include energy consumption, power utilisation, temperature set points, waste-heat utilisation, water usage and renewable-energy use. The rule is an operational/reporting workstream and should not be confused with an Irish grid-connection condition.

title.en: EU electronic sustainability label and minimum performance standards: do not assume final status

applicability.scope: Data centres potentially subject to an EU-wide future rating scheme and/or future minimum performance standards.
thresholds: The March 2026 Commission notice describes a draft second-step rating regulation; it is not itself a final Official Journal legal act.
The 2024/1364 regulation is the first-phase reporting and KPI measure.
location_conditions: The proposed rating was described as EU-wide and electronic labels were to be issued via the European database.

screening_logic.rule: Use an electronic label or mandatory rating as a future-regulation watch item unless a current Official Journal citation establishing the final second-step rule is attached. Never cite a policy-package announcement as the legal act.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: If a user or source claims that an EU rating, label or minimum-performance standard is already mandatory but cannot supply a later final legal citation, label the claim VERIFY / legal-status uncertainty.
screening_logic.agent_action: Monitor EUR-Lex and the Commission’s energy-performance page. At each release, supersede this record with a new in-force record that gives the definitive legal act, application date, metrics and transitional provisions.

content.en: The European Commission’s 27 March 2026 notice states that Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 was the first step: it established the European database and reporting scheme to collect information and KPIs for a future EU rating scheme. The notice described a draft second-step regulation, then open for feedback, under which electronic labels would be issued automatically by the European database, with adoption scheduled for the second quarter of 2026. Separately, the Commission’s current energy-performance page says that a future Data Centre Energy Efficiency Package will introduce a rating scheme and launch work on minimum performance standards. A draft, a planned adoption date or a generic ‘tech sovereignty package’ reference is not a substitute for a final Official Journal citation. This RAG record must be refreshed if a subsequent regulation is published.

title.en: National Biomethane Strategy: 5.7 TWh policy target

record.authority: Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment; Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine

applicability.scope: Irish biomethane-sector policy relevant to a data-centre project only where the project’s fuel, heat or dispatchable-generation strategy relies on indigenous biomethane.
thresholds: Government commitment to support delivery of up to 5.7 TWh of indigenously produced biomethane by 2030.
The strategy is a policy and regulatory roadmap for a biomethane industry at scale, with 25 strategic actions.
location_conditions: The strategy concerns biomethane produced in Ireland; it does not identify particular data-centre sites or create an electricity-network connection entitlement.

screening_logic.rule: When a site’s resilience, heat or fuel strategy claims a link to indigenous biomethane, record the 5.7 TWh target as a policy-context opportunity only. Assess actual fuel availability, connection capacity, contractual deliverability, emissions treatment and permits separately.
screening_logic.outcome_if_not_met: Absence of a biomethane route does not cause a failure of the CRU electricity connection test. Conversely, a national target does not prove supply is available to a particular site.
screening_logic.agent_action: Do not count this policy target towards the 80% renewable-electricity requirement unless the applicable electricity rule explicitly permits the calculation. Trigger a distinct gas/fuel due-diligence workstream.

content.en: Ireland’s National Biomethane Strategy states that the Government is committed to supporting delivery of up to 5.7 TWh of indigenously produced biomethane by 2030. It sets out policy and regulatory measures and a roadmap for an Irish biomethane industry at scale. This is a national energy and fuel policy target. It is not, by itself, a CRU electricity connection criterion for data centres, does not create a guaranteed fuel supply for a site, and does not establish a biomethane preference in CRU/2025236.
